name: Avatar
propertyCopy: Size, shape and initials text are properties of the same component, not separate avatars - change them below to check this avatar's types and presence states in the Live Preview.
guide: Component Guide Human View Machine View Overview Avatar represents a person throughout the product - in a profile menu, a comment, a team list, or an assignee indicator - a compact circular (or square) visual identifier shown as an image, initials, or a generic icon placeholder. When to Use A user profile menu or comment author - identifying who's associated with an action or piece of content. A team member list or an assignee indicator - showing who's involved at a glance. A chat participant list - compact identification across many people at once. When Not to Use Representing something that isn't a person or team - use Image or an icon instead - Avatar specifically implies identity. A context where a full name is more useful than a small visual - pair Avatar with a name rather than relying on the image alone when precision matters. A large, detailed profile photo display - use Image - Avatar is built for small, compact identification, not a full photo viewer. Best Practices Fall back to initials or a generic icon gracefully when no photo is available, rather than showing a broken image. Keep sizing consistent within any one context (all comments the same avatar size, for example). Use the presence/status dot sparingly and only when online/away/offline genuinely matters in that context. Do and Don't Do JD Two solid initials at a size that stays legible, with presence shown as a small status dot rather than competing text. Don't JOHNATHAN A full name crammed into a 40px circle is unreadable at any size. Avatars carry one or two initials - use a name label beside it for the rest. Accessibility Carries an accessible name identifying the person ("Jordan Lee's avatar" or simply the person's name), not left unlabeled. A presence dot's meaning (online/away/offline) is exposed in text or an accessible label, not communicated by color alone. Initials fallback text meets sufficient contrast against its background circle.
